# Parquet pushdown — in-browser perf sandbox

A focused A/B testbed for cold-start fetch performance against the canonical S3 parquets via DuckDB-WASM. We measure wall-clock time across a small matrix of {target, lever} so the wins (and losses) are direct and comparable. Every cold-lever run cache-busts its URL so the parquet has to be re-fetched.

## Why this exists

The dispatch series (`2026-05-25_parquet-pushdown-sandbox.md`) tracked a ~70 s cold-start fetch in the production Climate Rationale notebook. Two competing hypotheses:

- **H1 — parquet shape.** Canonical parquets ship with one giant row group + NULL filter-column stats → DuckDB-WASM can't skip work and pulls the whole file.
- **H2 — query shape.** The notebook's query is shaped in a way that defeats pushdown (no predicate, wrong column name, aliasing through views) even though the parquet itself is fine.

The pipeline-side STAGE D log + the single-file matrix below reject H1: predicate pushdown works on the canonical files. This sandbox is now repurposed to isolate **which query shapes win vs lose**, so we can fix production without a rebake. The CR-090 multi-file alias test at the bottom is the next probe.

## How to use it

1. **Optional**: open Chrome devtools → Network tab → filter `digital-atlas`, tick "Disable cache" + "Preserve log".
2. Click **Run all** under "Runner — single-file matrix". Each query writes a row to the table as it completes — rows stream in over ~3 min on a normal connection.
3. Read the **Verdict** block (auto-computed once all 10 queries finish).
4. Click **Run alias test** under "Multi-file alias test (CR-090)" to check whether `WHERE timeperiod = ...` (aliased) is slower than `WHERE period = ...` (raw partition column) on a 4-file `parquet_scan(...)` view — the leading hypothesis for the residual notebook pain.

Wall-clock times jitter 1.5–2× between re-runs because of S3 latency. Compare ratios, not absolute timings.

## The five levers we run per target

```{ojs}
// Multi-iso3 sample list for L7 — 5 representative African countries.
// Larger than typical (most production queries are 1-3 iso3s) so the
// row-group-skip stress is visible.
multiIso = ["AGO", "BFA", "CIV", "KEN", "NGA"];

perfLevers = [
  {
    key: "L2_cold_select_cols",
    label: "Cold • projection",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: ["SET enable_object_cache = true", "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"],
    hypothesis: "No predicate, explicit columns. Forces a full-file scan of just those columns — the worst-case query shape that still applies projection pushdown.",
    sqlTemplate: "SELECT <cols> FROM read_parquet('<url>')",
    query: (t, url) => `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}')`
  },
  {
    key: "L3_cold_cols_predicate",
    label: "Cold • single-iso3 predicate",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: ["SET enable_object_cache = true", "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"],
    hypothesis: "Projection + WHERE iso3 = '<one>'. Row-group skipping should fire if the parquet has usable per-row-group iso3 stats.",
    sqlTemplate: "SELECT <cols> FROM read_parquet('<url>') WHERE <isoCol> = '<sampleIso>'",
    query: (t, url) =>
      `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}') WHERE ${t.isoCol} = '${t.sampleIso}'`
  },
  {
    key: "L7_cold_multi_iso_predicate",
    label: "Cold • multi-iso3 IN-list (5)",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: ["SET enable_object_cache = true", "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"],
    hypothesis: "Projection + WHERE iso3 IN (5 countries). If pushdown degrades on multi-value predicates, L7 will be measurably slower than L3 — relevant because production often uses multi-iso3 IN-lists.",
    sqlTemplate: "SELECT <cols> FROM read_parquet('<url>') WHERE <isoCol> IN (<5 iso3s>)",
    query: (t, url) =>
      `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}') WHERE ${t.isoCol} IN (${multiIso.map(s => `'${s}'`).join(", ")})`
  },
  {
    key: "L4_cold_metadata_only",
    label: "Cold • parquet_metadata()",
    cacheBust: true,
    pragmas: ["SET enable_object_cache = true", "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"],
    hypothesis: "Cold-fetch floor: just the parquet footer. L3 / L7 cannot beat this.",
    sqlTemplate: "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM parquet_metadata('<url>')",
    query: (t, url) => `SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_groups FROM parquet_metadata('${url}')`
  },
  {
    key: "L5_warm_cols_predicate",
    label: "Warm • single-iso3 (re-uses L3 URL)",
    cacheBust: true,
    reuseCbOf: "L3_cold_cols_predicate",
    pragmas: ["SET enable_object_cache = true", "SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true"],
    hypothesis: "Warm reference: same SQL as L3, same cache-bust suffix as L3 → identical URL → object cache hits. Production users get this on any query AFTER the first against a given file.",
    sqlTemplate: "SELECT <cols> FROM read_parquet('<url>') WHERE <isoCol> = '<sampleIso>' (same url as L3)",
    query: (t, url) =>
      `SELECT ${t.cols.join(", ")} FROM read_parquet('${url}') WHERE ${t.isoCol} = '${t.sampleIso}'`
  }
];
```

## Setup

```{ojs}
import { patchWindowsCache } from "/helpers/data.js";
```

```{ojs}
sandboxDb = await DuckDBClient.of();
```

```{ojs}
// Single-row runner — re-used by both the single-file matrix and L6.
// Snapshots resource-timing entries around the query so http_reqs /
// http_bytes get attributed when the browser exposes them (it doesn't
// always — DuckDB-WASM worker fetches can bypass window.performance).
async function runOne(db, target, lever, runNonce) {
  // For warm-reference levers, reuse the cache-bust suffix of an earlier
  // lever so the URL is identical → DuckDB's object cache hits. Without
  // this, "warm" levers cache-bust to a fresh URL and are actually cold.
  const cbKey = lever.reuseCbOf ?? lever.key;
  const cb = lever.cacheBust ? `?cb=${runNonce}_${cbKey}` : "";
  const url = patchWindowsCache(target.url) + cb;

  for (const p of lever.pragmas) {
    await db.query(p);
  }

  const sql = lever.query(target, url);

  const beforeEntries = performance.getEntriesByType("resource");
  const beforeCount = beforeEntries.length;
  const t0 = performance.now();
  let rowsReturned = null;
  let errored = null;
  try {
    const resp = await db.query(sql);
    rowsReturned = (resp && typeof resp.length === "number")
      ? resp.length
      : (resp && resp.numRows) ?? null;
  } catch (e) {
    errored = String(e && e.message || e);
  }
  const t1 = performance.now();

  const entries = performance.getEntriesByType("resource").slice(beforeCount);
  const targetHost = "digital-atlas.s3.amazonaws.com";
  const matched = entries.filter((e) => e.name.includes(targetHost));
  const bytes = matched.reduce(
    (a, e) => a + (e.transferSize || e.encodedBodySize || 0),
    0
  );

  return {
    target: target.key,
    lever: lever.label,
    leverKey: lever.key,
    query_ms: errored == null ? Math.round(t1 - t0) : null,
    http_reqs: matched.length,
    http_bytes: bytes,
    rows_returned: rowsReturned,
    error: errored
  };
}
```

## Runner — single-file matrix

```{ojs}
viewof runNonce = Inputs.button([
  ["Run all", () => Date.now()],
  ["Re-run (new cache-bust)", () => Date.now()],
  ["Clear results", () => 0]
], { value: 0, label: "Action" })
```

```{ojs}
mutable streamRows = [];
```

```{ojs}
mutable streamStatus = "Idle — click 'Run all' to populate the table.";
```

```{ojs}
// Async runner. Uses a LOCAL `acc` array as the source of truth and
// publishes snapshots via `mutable streamRows = acc`. Critically does NOT
// read `streamRows` inside this cell — Observable would treat that as a
// dependency and re-execute the cell on every mutable write, causing a
// runaway loop (and the visible "page flashing" symptom).
streamRunner = {
  const nonce = runNonce;
  if (!nonce) {
    mutable streamRows = [];
    mutable streamStatus = "Idle — click 'Run all' to populate the table.";
    return null;
  }
  let acc = [];
  mutable streamRows = acc;
  let i = 0;
  const total = perfTargets.length * perfLevers.length;
  for (const target of perfTargets) {
    for (const lever of perfLevers) {
      i++;
      mutable streamStatus = `Running ${i}/${total} — ${target.key} • ${lever.label}…`;
      try {
        const r = await runOne(sandboxDb, target, lever, nonce);
        acc = [...acc, r];
        mutable streamRows = acc;
      } catch (e) {
        acc = [...acc, {
          target: target.key,
          lever: lever.label,
          leverKey: lever.key,
          query_ms: null,
          http_reqs: 0,
          http_bytes: 0,
          rows_returned: null,
          error: String(e)
        }];
        mutable streamRows = acc;
      }
    }
  }
  mutable streamStatus = `Done — ${total} runs completed at ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}.`;
  return acc;
}
```

## Verdict — single-file pushdown (auto-computed)

```{ojs}
{
  const total = perfTargets.length * perfLevers.length;
  if (streamRows.length < total) {
    return htl.html`<p style="color: #888; font-style: italic;">Verdict will appear once all ${total} levers complete.</p>`;
  }

  // Bucket by target.
  const byTarget = new Map();
  for (const r of streamRows) {
    if (!byTarget.has(r.target)) byTarget.set(r.target, {});
    byTarget.get(r.target)[r.leverKey] = r;
  }

  const verdicts = [];
  for (const [targetKey, levers] of byTarget) {
    const l2 = levers.L2_cold_select_cols;
    const l3 = levers.L3_cold_cols_predicate;
    const l7 = levers.L7_cold_multi_iso_predicate;
    const l4 = levers.L4_cold_metadata_only;
    const l5 = levers.L5_warm_cols_predicate;
    // Headline: L2 (no predicate) -> L3 (single-iso3 predicate). This is
    // the direct measurement of how much predicate pushdown buys you.
    const r23 = l2 && l3 && l2.query_ms && l3.query_ms ? (l2.query_ms / l3.query_ms) : null;
    // Single -> multi-iso3 cost. > 1 means the IN-list slows things down.
    const r37 = l3 && l7 && l3.query_ms && l7.query_ms ? (l7.query_ms / l3.query_ms) : null;
    // How close L3 is to the cold-fetch floor.
    const r34 = l3 && l4 && l3.query_ms && l4.query_ms ? (l3.query_ms / l4.query_ms) : null;
    // Warm speedup.
    const r35 = l3 && l5 && l3.query_ms && l5.query_ms ? (l3.query_ms / l5.query_ms) : null;

    let verdict;
    let color;
    if (r23 == null) {
      verdict = "errored — see the table";
      color = "#b00";
    } else if (r23 >= 5) {
      verdict = `Predicate pushdown WORKING — ${r23.toFixed(1)}× speedup from adding WHERE iso3. No rebake needed for this target.`;
      color = "#080";
    } else if (r23 >= 2) {
      verdict = `Predicate pushdown PARTIAL — ${r23.toFixed(1)}× speedup. Row-group skipping is firing but moderately; possibly some iso3s are spread across many row groups.`;
      color = "#a60";
    } else {
      verdict = `Predicate pushdown BLOCKED — ${r23.toFixed(1)}× speedup only. The parquet has one giant row group or NULL stats on iso3.`;
      color = "#b00";
    }

    // Note on multi-iso3 if available.
    let multiNote = null;
    if (r37 != null) {
      if (r37 >= 2) {
        multiNote = htl.html`<div style="margin-top: 4px; color: #a60; font-size: 0.85rem;">⚠ Multi-iso3 IN-list is ${r37.toFixed(1)}× slower than single-iso3. Production queries with multi-country selection will pay this.</div>`;
      } else if (r37 >= 1.3) {
        multiNote = htl.html`<div style="margin-top: 4px; color: #888; font-size: 0.85rem;">Multi-iso3 IN-list is ${r37.toFixed(1)}× slower than single-iso3 — modest cost from touching more row groups.</div>`;
      } else {
        multiNote = htl.html`<div style="margin-top: 4px; color: #888; font-size: 0.85rem;">Multi-iso3 IN-list is ${r37.toFixed(1)}× the single-iso3 cost — pushdown handles IN-lists efficiently here.</div>`;
      }
    }

    verdicts.push(htl.html`<div style="margin: 0 0 12px 0; padding: 10px 14px; background: #fafafa; border-left: 4px solid ${color}; font-size: 0.9rem;">
      <div style="font-weight: 600; font-family: monospace;">${targetKey}</div>
      <div style="margin-top: 4px;"><strong style="color: ${color};">${verdict}</strong></div>
      ${multiNote ?? ""}
      <div style="margin-top: 6px; color: #555; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.82rem;">
        L2=${l2?.query_ms ?? "—"}ms · L3=${l3?.query_ms ?? "—"}ms · L7=${l7?.query_ms ?? "—"}ms · L4=${l4?.query_ms ?? "—"}ms · L5=${l5?.query_ms ?? "—"}ms
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top: 4px; color: #555; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.82rem;">
        L2→L3 = ${r23 ? r23.toFixed(1) + "×" : "—"} (single-iso3 predicate) ·
        L3→L7 = ${r37 ? r37.toFixed(1) + "×" : "—"} (cost of multi-iso3) ·
        L3→L5 = ${r35 ? r35.toFixed(1) + "×" : "—"} (warm speedup) ·
        L3→L4 = ${r34 ? r34.toFixed(1) + "×" : "—"} (headroom to floor)
      </div>
    </div>`);
  }

  return htl.html`<div>${verdicts}</div>`;
}
```

## Multi-file alias test (CR-090 hypothesis)

The production `dbFutureHive` cell creates a view aliasing `period → timeperiod` over a 4-file `parquet_scan(..., hive_partitioning=1)`:

```sql
CREATE VIEW futureProjections AS
  SELECT *, period AS timeperiod
  FROM parquet_scan([4 paths], hive_partitioning = 1)
```

Consumer queries then filter `WHERE timeperiod = '2021-2040'`. If hive-partition pruning needs the raw column name `period` (not the alias) to do file-list elimination, the view scans all 4 files per query — a ~4× slowdown on top of the per-file L3 cost.

This test runs the same query twice with different cache-bust salts so both runs are cold:

- **L6a**: `WHERE period = '2021-2040'` (raw partition column)
- **L6b**: `WHERE timeperiod = '2021-2040'` (aliased via view)

If L6b is ≥3× slower than L6a, the alias is the bug and the production fix is to drop the alias from the view definition.

```{ojs}
cmip6Periods = [
  "s3://digital-atlas/domain=climate/type=hazard-indices/source=nex-gddp-cmip6/region=africa/processing=timeseries_mean_month/timeframe=3months/period=2021-2040/baseline=1995-2014/variable=ensemble_season_timeseries.parquet",
  "s3://digital-atlas/domain=climate/type=hazard-indices/source=nex-gddp-cmip6/region=africa/processing=timeseries_mean_month/timeframe=3months/period=2041-2060/baseline=1995-2014/variable=ensemble_season_timeseries.parquet",
  "s3://digital-atlas/domain=climate/type=hazard-indices/source=nex-gddp-cmip6/region=africa/processing=timeseries_mean_month/timeframe=3months/period=2061-2080/baseline=1995-2014/variable=ensemble_season_timeseries.parquet",
  "s3://digital-atlas/domain=climate/type=hazard-indices/source=nex-gddp-cmip6/region=africa/processing=timeseries_mean_month/timeframe=3months/period=2081-2100/baseline=1995-2014/variable=ensemble_season_timeseries.parquet"
];
```

```{ojs}
aliasRunner = {
  const nonce = aliasRunNonce;
  if (!nonce) {
    mutable aliasResults = null;
    mutable aliasStatus = "Idle — click 'Run alias test' to begin.";
    return null;
  }
  mutable aliasResults = null;
  await sandboxDb.query(`SET enable_object_cache = true`);
  await sandboxDb.query(`SET enable_http_metadata_cache = true`);

  const out = {};

  // L6a: raw partition column
  mutable aliasStatus = "L6a — WHERE period = '2021-2040' (raw column)…";
  const urlsA = cmip6Periods.map((u, i) => `'${patchWindowsCache(u)}?cb=${nonce}_alias_raw_${i}'`).join(", ");
  await sandboxDb.query(`DROP VIEW IF EXISTS futureProj_raw`);
  await sandboxDb.query(`CREATE VIEW futureProj_raw AS SELECT * FROM parquet_scan([${urlsA}], hive_partitioning = 1)`);
  const t0a = performance.now();
  let respA = null;
  let errA = null;
  try {
    respA = await sandboxDb.query(
      `SELECT iso3, scenario, season, year, mean FROM futureProj_raw WHERE iso3 = 'AGO' AND period = '2021-2040'`
    );
  } catch (e) {
    errA = String(e && e.message || e);
  }
  const t1a = performance.now();
  out.raw = {
    label: "L6a — WHERE period (raw)",
    ms: Math.round(t1a - t0a),
    rows: respA?.length ?? null,
    error: errA
  };
  mutable aliasResults = { ...out };

  // L6b: aliased
  mutable aliasStatus = "L6b — WHERE timeperiod = '2021-2040' (aliased)…";
  const urlsB = cmip6Periods.map((u, i) => `'${patchWindowsCache(u)}?cb=${nonce}_alias_aliased_${i}'`).join(", ");
  await sandboxDb.query(`DROP VIEW IF EXISTS futureProj_aliased`);
  await sandboxDb.query(`CREATE VIEW futureProj_aliased AS SELECT *, period AS timeperiod FROM parquet_scan([${urlsB}], hive_partitioning = 1)`);
  const t0b = performance.now();
  let respB = null;
  let errB = null;
  try {
    respB = await sandboxDb.query(
      `SELECT iso3, scenario, season, year, mean FROM futureProj_aliased WHERE iso3 = 'AGO' AND timeperiod = '2021-2040'`
    );
  } catch (e) {
    errB = String(e && e.message || e);
  }
  const t1b = performance.now();
  out.aliased = {
    label: "L6b — WHERE timeperiod (aliased)",
    ms: Math.round(t1b - t0b),
    rows: respB?.length ?? null,
    error: errB
  };
  mutable aliasResults = { ...out };
  mutable aliasStatus = `Done — completed at ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}.`;
  return out;
}
```

```{ojs}
htl.html`<div style="padding: 8px 12px; background: #f7f7f7; border-left: 3px solid #888; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; margin: 8px 0;">${aliasStatus}</div>`
```

```{ojs}
{
  if (!aliasResults || (!aliasResults.raw && !aliasResults.aliased)) {

  let verdict = null;
  if (aliasResults.raw && aliasResults.aliased && aliasResults.raw.ms && aliasResults.aliased.ms) {
    const ratio = aliasResults.aliased.ms / aliasResults.raw.ms;
    let color, msg;
    if (ratio >= 3) {
      color = "#b00";
      msg = `ALIAS BREAKS PUSHDOWN — aliased query is ${ratio.toFixed(1)}× slower. Fix: drop the alias in the view, or filter on raw 'period' in the consumer.`;
    } else if (ratio >= 1.5) {
      color = "#a60";
      msg = `Alias somewhat slower (${ratio.toFixed(1)}×). Likely some pushdown loss; worth fixing but not the primary 70 s contributor.`;
    } else {
      color = "#080";
      msg = `Alias is fine (${ratio.toFixed(1)}×). The 70 s notebook pain must be elsewhere (multi-iso3 IN-list, mainGaul lookup, or session warm-up cost).`;
    }
    verdict = htl.html`<div style="margin: 10px 0; padding: 10px 14px; background: #fafafa; border-left: 4px solid ${color}; font-size: 0.9rem;">
      <strong style="color: ${color};">${msg}</strong>
    </div>`;
  }
  return htl.html`<div>
    <table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 0.9rem; margin-top: 8px;">
      <thead><tr style="background: #f3f3f3; text-align: left;">
        <th style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc;">Variant</th>

        <td style="padding: 6px 8px;">${r.label}</td>
```

## Read the table (verbose diagnostics)

- **L2 vs L3** — L2 is "no predicate" (full file scan, just projection); L3 adds `WHERE iso3 = '<one>'`. The ratio is the direct measurement of predicate pushdown. ≥5× = pushdown working; 2–5× = partial (likely iso3 spread across many row groups); <2× = blocked (one giant row group or NULL stats).
- **L3 vs L7** — single-iso3 vs 5-iso3 IN-list. If L7 ≈ L3, DuckDB handles multi-value predicates efficiently. If L7 ≫ L3, row-group skipping degrades on IN-lists — relevant because production queries often select multiple countries.
- **L4** is the cold-fetch floor (just the parquet footer). L3 cannot beat it. The L3→L4 ratio shows how much headroom is left from L3 to the file's minimum cost.
- **L5** is the warm-cache reference — same SQL as L3 but reuses L3's URL so DuckDB's object cache hits. Production users get this on any query AFTER the first against a given file. L3→L5 = the warm speedup factor.

## Known limitations

- **`Bytes downloaded` reads 0 in this host** — DuckDB-WASM routes parquet fetches through a worker that doesn't surface to `window.performance.getEntriesByType("resource")`. Use Chrome devtools → Network → filter `digital-atlas` for ground-truth byte counts. Query time is the source of truth here.
- **Re-runs jitter 1.5–2×** because of S3 latency variance. The L1→L3 ratio per re-run is reliable; the absolute ms numbers are not.
- **L5 warm column** should be ~300 ms when it actually hits the cache (verified for both targets after the `reuseCbOf` fix that makes L5 reuse L3's URL). Partly real (`object_cache` hit) and partly DuckDB's internal result cache. Don't over-interpret the absolute number — it's a sanity floor for "warm".

## Out of scope

- Canonical-vs-rebake A/B against `s3://digital-atlas/sandbox/parquet-pushdown/...`. Pipeline-side STAGE D verdict (`hazards_prototype/logs/Dpush_speedup_20260525_121356.log`) already ruled the rebake out — 0/9 targets at ≥3× speedup. The sandbox-prefix files are kept for now (negligible cost) but won't be promoted.
- Promotion commands (STAGE F). See parent dispatch.
- `mainGaul` lookup investigation (CR-089) — that's a separate notebook-side fix, not a pushdown question. Promoted to leading suspect for the residual 70 s pain after CR-090 was rejected by the alias test.
- Production query shapes with multi-column predicates (`AND season = ...`, `AND scenario IN (...)`, OR-clauses). The sandbox stays focused on the single-axis iso3 predicate; if L7 shows IN-list cost is high, build a follow-up matrix.
